findings.title: Upload poll loop has no disconnectedCallback; terminal event dispatched from a detached node never reaches the model-run picker
findings.suggested_fix: Add a disconnectedCallback that sets a `this._stopped = true` flag (or uses an AbortController) and check it at the top of each `_await` loop iteration, returning without touching `this._statusEl`/`this._progressEl` if the element has been removed. Concrete interleaving: `_upload()` enters `_await(job)` and is mid-`setTimeout` when `<ngiab-upload-run>` is removed from the document (e.g. a future re-render, or the component test's `el.remove()` in afterEach while a poll is still pending). Nothing stops the loop; two seconds later `appAPI.uploadStatus` resolves, `this._say(...)` writes to a detached `_statusEl` (silently a no-op the user never sees), and if the job is done, `this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('run-published', { bubbles: true, ... }))` is fired at line 129 from a node with no path to `document` -- bubbling events from a detached node never reach a `document`-level listener. `ngiab-model-runs`'s `document.addEventListener('run-published', ...)` (ngiab-model-runs.js:33) is therefore never invoked, so a successfully completed upload silently fails to appear in the run picker with no error surfaced anywhere. Even while still connected, the loop is also unbounded (see next finding).

findings.title: Upload XHR is not cancellable: the abort listener is wired but never reachable from the caller
findings.suggested_fix: `send()` (and `putPresigned`/`postToPortal`) only return the settlement Promise, never the `XMLHttpRequest` instance itself, so nothing outside `lib/upload.js` can ever call `request.abort()`. The `abort` event listener at line 19 is therefore dead code: no caller, including a future `disconnectedCallback` on `ngiab-upload-run`, has a handle to cancel an in-flight multi-gigabyte transfer if the user navigates away or the panel is torn down. Return `{ promise, abort: () => request.abort() }` (or accept an AbortSignal and wire `signal.addEventListener('abort', () => request.abort())`) so `ngiab-upload-run` can cancel the transfer on disconnect instead of leaving it running in the background.

findings.title: Status poll has no upper bound, timeout, or user-facing cancel
findings.suggested_fix: `for (;;)` polls every 2s forever until `status.terminal` is true. If the unpack worker crashes, the job is lost, or the server never marks the job terminal, the panel polls indefinitely with no timeout and no way for the user to cancel or retry short of reloading the page (which, per the finding above, would also silently orphan the request). Add a maximum attempt count or wall-clock timeout that surfaces a definite error state instead of polling forever.

findings.title: Overlapping refresh() calls on ngiab-model-runs can resolve out of order and clobber a fresher run list
findings.suggested_fix: `refresh()` has three independent call sites that can fire close together: the initial `connectedCallback` call (line 35), the `run-published` document listener (line 32-33, fired whenever an upload finishes), and the post-delete call inside `_remove()` (line 126). None of them are serialized or tagged with a sequence token/AbortController, so two in-flight `appAPI.getModelRuns()` requests can resolve out of order. Concrete interleaving: user deletes a run (`_remove()` awaits `removeModelRun`, then calls `refresh()` at line 126) while, moments earlier, an upload finished and its `run-published` handler already kicked off its own `refresh()`. If the run-published `refresh()`'s GET is still in flight (started before the delete) and resolves after the delete's own `refresh()` GET (started after, but answered faster), the stale response -- which still lists the just-deleted run -- overwrites `_selectEl` and silently 'un-deletes' it from the picker until the next refresh. Add a monotonically increasing request token: capture it before the `await`, and ignore the response in the `.then`/post-await branch if a newer refresh has since started.

residual_risks: lib/upload.js: if `transfer.putPresigned` succeeds but the subsequent `appAPI.startUpload` (ngiab-upload-run.js:88) fails, the archive is already in the bucket and a job was reserved, but the server is never told to start it. Retrying with the same name may then be rejected by the server as a duplicate, or leave an orphaned job/bytes in storage. This is primarily a backend cleanup concern rather than a pure client race, but the frontend gives the user no way to resume or explicitly abandon that half-finished job -- clicking Upload again just starts a brand-new `createUpload`.

config.js: `canUpload()`/`canSeeDelete()` are read once at `connectedCallback` time and never re-checked; if a session's permissions change server-side mid-visit (e.g. a role revoked), the panel does not reflect it until a full page reload. This is expected for a server-rendered config snapshot and not itself a bug, but is worth confirming is the intended contract.
testing_gaps: No test in ngiab-upload-run.test.js disconnects the element (`el.remove()`) while a poll is pending to verify the loop stops touching the DOM and the `run-published` event is not silently lost -- exactly the scenario every other test's `afterEach` performs after settling, but never mid-poll.

No test exercises two `ngiab-model-runs.refresh()` calls resolving out of order (e.g. stubbing `appAPI.getModelRuns` to resolve the second call before the first) to confirm the run picker converges on the latest data rather than the latest-arriving response.
No test verifies that an in-flight upload's XHR is aborted (or at least that no further progress/status callback fires) if the panel is removed from the DOM before the transfer completes.
